name: MetroPT
description: The paper describes the MetroPT data set, an outcome of a eXplainable Predictive Maintenance (XPM) project with an urban metro public transportation service in Porto, Portugal. The data was collected in 2022 that aimed to evaluate machine learning methods for online anomaly detection and failure prediction. By capturing several analogic sensor signals (pressure, temperature, current consumption), digital signals (control signals, discrete signals), and GPS information (latitude, longitude, and speed), we provide a dataset that can be easily used to evaluate online machine learning methods. This dataset contains some interesting characteristics and can be a good benchmark for predictive maintenance models.
typical_sota_score: 60–90% (F1, varies by task and evaluation split)
reputation: A recent real-world predictive maintenance dataset that has been used as a practical benchmark for online anomaly detection and failure prediction in industrial settings.
notes: Non-LLM, multivariate sensor time-series benchmark with class imbalance and strong temporal dependence; results can vary substantially by preprocessing and event-window definition.
